summary.title: How to Make Your First Roguelike
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a simple, playable browser roguelike in JavaScript and Phaser, covering random ASCII maps, turn-based movement and combat, and basic enemy AI.
takeaways: Generate a random tile map where walls block movement and floors are walkable, using simple procedural generation.
Track actors with a list and a position-keyed lookup map so movement and combat can find occupants quickly.
Handle movement and attacks in one function: moving into an actor attacks it, and it dies when HP reaches zero.
Implement simple enemy AI: chase the player when within six steps, otherwise wander randomly.
Add win and lose messages, then extend the game with levels, power-ups, inventory, consumables, or equipment.
summary.summary: This tutorial walks through building a traditional roguelike (single-player, randomized, turn-based dungeon crawler with permadeath) in JavaScript using the HTML5 engine Phaser. It builds the game step by step: ASCII rendering on a text grid, random 80% wall maps, actor setup, blocking checks, a moveTo() function that handles both movement and attacks, and an AI that pursues the player within six steps. The author also notes a Haxe version of the code is included in the source download.
